hints: Focus on what happens to the ammonia equilibrium if you change its pressure or remove one of its reactants.
Opening tap 1 lets the gases expand into an evacuated vessel, so total pressure falls, while opening tap 2 lets nitrogen reach lithium and be removed as solid $\text{Li}_3\text{N}$.
Apply Le Chatelier to each change and ask which combination avoids shifting the $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$ equilibrium to the left.
walkthrough:
**Recall the equilibrium in the middle vessel**

Think of the middle vessel as happy where it is. It contains:

$$\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$$

Anything that lowers pressure or removes $\text{N}_2$ or $\text{H}_2$ will push it left and destroy $\text{NH}_3$.

**Consider opening tap 1 to the evacuated vessel**

Opening to a second equal volume doubles the volume for the gases, so partial pressures all fall. There are 4 moles of gas on the left and only 2 moles on the right, so lower pressure favours the left side.

This shift to the left decreases ammonia.

**Consider opening tap 2 to the lithium vessel**

Lithium reacts at room temperature with nitrogen:

$$6\text{Li}(\text{s}) + \text{N}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{Li}_3\text{N}(\text{s})$$

This permanently removes $\text{N}_2$ gas from the equilibrium mixture. To replace the lost reactant, the ammonia equilibrium shifts left, $2\text{NH}_3$ breaking down to $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2$.

This also decreases ammonia.

**Compare all four actions**

Keeping both taps closed causes no change, so no left shift occurs. Opening either tap causes a left shift, and opening both causes both harmful effects together. Therefore doing nothing preserves the most $\text{NH}_3$.

options.A: With both taps closed the volume, pressure and amounts of N2, H2 and NH3 stay as they were at equilibrium. No Le Chatelier shift to the left is triggered, so the amount of ammonia remains highest.
options.B: This combines both damaging effects. Expansion into the left vessel lowers pressure and favours 4 moles to 2 moles shift left, while lithium on the right removes N2 as Li3N and also pulls the equilibrium left. Ammonia is lowest here.
options.C: Opening tap 1 only lets the equilibrium gases expand into the evacuated vessel. Total pressure drops, so the equilibrium shifts toward more gas moles, to the left toward N2 + 3H2. Ammonia decreases by dilution and by shift.
options.D: Opening tap 2 only lets N2 diffuse to Li and form solid Li3N. Removing a reactant N2 causes the N2 + 3H2 reversible reaction to shift left to try to replace it, decomposing NH3. Ammonia therefore falls.
